issues.description: The template and solution differ in the return type of Course.addRating(stars:). The problem statement describes only the behavior (validate and add rating) and does not specify a return type. In the template the method is declared as a Void function (func addRating(stars: Int) { ... }) while the solution implements it as returning a Bool (func addRating(stars: Int) -> Bool { ... }). This mismatch is structural (different signatures) and can confuse students about whether they should return a success flag or not; it can also lead to subtle test/signature mismatches if the tests or reference use the Bool return in the future.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the addRating(stars:) signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the template to declare the method as returning Bool (func addRating(stars: Int) -> Bool) and document in the problem statement that the method should return true on successful addition and false on invalid input, or (B) change the solution to a Void return (func addRating(stars: Int)) so it matches the template and problem statement. Prefer option A if you want to keep the informative success/failure return value used in the solution; otherwise explicitly state in the problem that no return value is required to avoid ambiguity.
